notes: ACCESS: Tier 1 (direct HTTP via curl and WebFetch) was blocked immediately on every page fetch (homepage, category page) by PerimeterX (HTTP 429 / px-captcha challenge page) -- first real block, so moved to Tier 3 (Claude-in-Chrome; no separate Playwright/CDP tool exists in this environment) per the hard-block rule. robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (checked: no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web/Claude-User/Claude-SearchBot rules), so browser automation was permitted. Sitemaps (seo-category-index.xml -> seo-category-sitemap~0.xml, 158 top-level 'cat' URLs) WERE reachable via plain curl (not blocked), and were used to discover the single top-level 'Holiday' category node (https://www.jossandmain.com/holiday/cat/holiday-c1863391.html) before switching to the browser for sub-category discovery, counts and verification. DISCOVERY: Joss & Main (Wayfair-owned; investigated independently of AllModern/Birch Lane per instructions) has ONE seasonal hub in its main taxonomy: 'Holiday' (not in the visible top nav bar, but present in the sitemap and reachable directly; page itself is a genuine PLP with sort/filter and 1,683 total items, hero imagery is a Christmas mantel/tree/gift scene). Its own left-nav/tile carousel lists exactly 10 children (confirmed via 'Items 1 through X of 10' pagination and via DOM read of each tile's href): Christmas Trees, Holiday Wreaths, Tree Skirts & Collars, Stockings & Stocking Holders, Ornaments & Tree Toppers, Holiday Decorative Accents, Garlands, Tree & Novelty Garlands, Holiday Lights, Hanukkah. All except 'Garlands' live under the /holiday/sb0/... URL namespace with breadcrumb 'Holiday / <name>', confirming they are genuine holiday-specific PLPs; content across them (trees, ornaments, tree skirts, stockings, mantel/wreath decor, string lights) is uniformly Christmas-context product, so category was normalized to 'Christmas' for these 8 (the site itself only labels the umbrella 'Holiday', and the discovery vocabulary explicitly treats 'Holiday Decor'/'Holiday Decorations' as Christmas-family terms). 'Hanukkah' is an explicit, separately-named leaf category (own breadcrumb, own URL, 12 items) and was kept as its own category. EXCLUDED: (1) 'Garlands' tile on the Holiday hub resolves to https://www.jossandmain.com/decor-pillows/sb0/garlands-c1859254.html with breadcrumb 'Decor & Pillows / Botanicals / Garlands' (243 items) -- its canonical taxonomic home is the general Decor & Pillows > Botanicals branch, not Holiday; it is a general product-type category merely cross-linked/shortcut from the Holiday landing page, not a holiday-specific PLP (rules 5-6: product type living in a category does not make the category seasonal). The genuine holiday-specific garland leaf ('Tree & Novelty Garlands', 10 items, /holiday/sb0/ URL) was kept. (2) A site keyword search for 'halloween' (https://www.jossandmain.com/keyword.php?keyword=halloween) returns a dynamic 'Halloween' heading with 547 results, but it is a plain search-results endpoint with no breadcrumb and no dedicated category URL/slug -- excluded per the shared core's search-result-page rule; it does not indicate a genuine Halloween category exists in the taxonomy. NO_SEASONAL CHECK FOR OTHER HOLIDAYS: reviewed the complete rendered mega-menu (New, Furniture, Outdoor, Lighting, Decor & Pillows, Wall Decor & Mirrors, Rugs, Bedding, Bath, Kitchen & Tabletop, Storage, Reno, Sale, plus all Collections/Style/Room sub-panels) in full -- no Halloween, Easter, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, New Year, Diwali, or other festival branch appears anywhere outside the Holiday hub described above; grepped the full 158-URL category sitemap for halloween/easter/valentine/thanksgiving/diwali/new-year/hanukkah/holiday -- only the one 'holiday' URL matches. Concluding these holidays are absent from this site's own taxonomy (correct NO_SEASONAL outcome for each, not an error) rather than continuing to individual keyword searches, since the Halloween search test already demonstrated searches surface generic non-category results here. QTY METHOD: displayed 'N Items' PLP header on each sb0 page (site's own count), read via accessibility-tree text extraction, matches priority-1 method. Parent 'Holiday' (1,683 items) kept as a grouping-only row under 'Christmas' per the shared engine's never-double-count rule (sum of the 8 Christmas children = 1,440; children + Hanukkah = 1,452; the ~231-item gap to 1,683 is consistent with overlap from the excluded generic Garlands category, which is not separately counted here).
